prompt: A confident person walks forward with upright posture, clear heel-to-toe contacts, relaxed arm swing, and a balanced stop.
A hurried person walks forward quickly without running, leaning slightly into the motion, with controlled foot contacts and a clean stop.
A cautious person advances slowly with short careful steps, wary head movement, guarded posture, stable feet, and a quiet stop.
A person makes a short controlled run forward, accelerates naturally, takes energetic strides, decelerates, and recovers to balanced standing.
A person walks forward naturally for several steps, visibly decelerates, plants both feet, absorbs momentum, and settles into neutral standing.
A standing person anticipates, shifts weight, turns the entire body ninety degrees to the left with natural pivoting footwork, and settles with planted feet.
A person takes two clear lateral sidesteps to the left while keeping the torso generally forward, then plants both feet in a balanced stance.
A person takes two controlled steps backward while staying alert and facing forward, then stops with stable planted feet.
A person listens attentively in a relaxed neutral stance with subtle breathing, small responsive head motion, and a gentle weight shift.
A person listens impatiently, shifts weight, briefly folds and releases the arms, glances aside, and returns to a readable waiting stance.
A person talks casually with grounded posture, natural asymmetric hand gestures, responsive head movement, and both arms returning to rest.
A person responds defensively with a small backward weight shift, guarded torso, palms briefly raised, and a controlled recovery to neutral.
A person gives one clear full-body shrug with shoulders rising, elbows bending and palms turning outward, holds briefly, then relaxes completely.
A person has a small sudden startle: quick head and shoulder reaction, brief torso recoil, feet mostly planted, then a wary recovery.
A person reacts with a large readable full-body recoil, throws weight backward, raises the arms protectively, catches balance, and recovers.
A person looks at something, turns away, then snaps back for a clear comedic double take using head, shoulders, torso, and a small foot adjustment.
A confused person leans the upper body sideways to inspect around an obstruction, balances through hips and feet, then returns upright.
A person notices someone approaching, takes two purposeful steps sideways to clear a path, turns slightly toward them, and settles out of the way.
A person advances two steps into the space between two other people, squares the body to mediate, raises calming hands, and plants firmly.
A person leans and steps slightly around a blocking actor to see past them, leads with the head and shoulders, then returns to their mark.
